top_story.headline: House bill would bar candidates from betting on their own elections
top_story.dek: Rep. Donald Davis introduced the measure during a brief Monday House session that produced no votes.
paragraphs: H.R. 10732, introduced by Rep. Donald G. Davis (D-NC-1), would amend title 52 of the United States Code to prohibit candidates for federal office from trading in contracts on the outcome of their own elections. It was referred to the Committee on House Administration.
The Congressional Record lists no cosponsors on the bill. The bill targets candidates trading in contracts on their own election outcomes, an ethics and money-in-politics question.

The House met Monday, October 5, 2026, approved the Journal, received a message from the Senate, and adjourned at 4:33 p.m. until 4 p.m. Tuesday. The Congressional Record shows no recorded votes in the House that day.

sections.headline: Short House session, no votes; 41 bills and resolutions introduced
paragraphs: The House convened Monday, October 5, 2026, and adjourned at 4:33 p.m. until 4 p.m. Tuesday. The Congressional Record shows 30 House bills (H.R. 10721–10750) and 11 House resolutions (H.Res. 1606–1616) introduced. The Senate's only recorded action in the Congressional Record was adjournment until 1:30 p.m. Tuesday, October 6.

A message from the Senate read in the House announced Senate adoption of S. Res. 913, mourning the death of former Kansas Senator Nancy Kassebaum, and Senate passage of 21 bills awaiting House concurrence, among them S. 528 (reauthorizing the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative), S. 4395 (reauthorizing the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act of 2002) and S. 4668 (name, image and likeness protections for student athletes). The Senate also appointed Adam Klein of Texas to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act Reform Commission. The House Clerk, Kevin F. McCumber, reported that H.R. 5345, on a single point of contact at the Social Security Administration for identity-theft victims, was presented to the President on September 29, 2026.

Among the introductions, other newsworthy items include Rep. William Keating's Ukraine Temporary Protected Status bill (H.R. 10740) with dozens of bipartisan cosponsors, and Rep. Sharice Davids' package of seven health care bills. Many of the resolutions are commemorative designations.

items: H.R. 10721, sponsored by Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ-3) — requires sufficient bonding and timely cleanup of land and water disturbed by federal and Indian oil and gas production (Natural Resources).
H.R. 10722, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — expands behavioral health workforce training programs (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10723, sponsored by Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-6) — sets up a bilateral rapid-response protocol for serious crimes against U.S. citizens in Mexico (Foreign Affairs).
H.R. 10724, sponsored by Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA-46) — clarifies the bankruptcy rules on exceptions to discharge of an individual debtor's debts (Judiciary).
H.R. 10725, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — makes reforms to Medicare supplemental (Medigap) health insurance policies (Ways and Means, Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10726, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — lets people with Alzheimer's disease buy into Medicare (Ways and Means, Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10727, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — gives priority to expanding service applications from certain entities under the Public Health Service Act (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10728, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — exempts certain maternity, labor and delivery services from limits on state-directed Medicaid payments (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10729, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — adjusts limits on state-directed Medicaid payments and repeals certain provider-tax provisions of Public Law 119-21 (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10730, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — modifies the premium tax credit (Energy and Commerce, Ways and Means).
H.R. 10731, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — adjusts the Medicare cost pass-through for certified registered nurse anesthetists (Ways and Means).
H.R. 10732, sponsored by Rep. Donald G. Davis (D-NC-1) — prohibits candidates for federal office from trading in contracts on the outcome of their own elections (House Administration).
H.R. 10733, sponsored by Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-PA-4) — establishes a Science Advisory Board at the Department of Justice (Judiciary).
H.R. 10734, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-6) — sets standards of liability for sex-based harassment under Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (Education and Workforce).
H.R. 10735, sponsored by Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO-8) — requires certain types of cattle to be included in a livestock pilot program under the Federal Crop Insurance Act (Agriculture).
H.R. 10736, sponsored by Rep. Brad Finstad (R-MN-1) — bars federal acquisitions of computers or printers from entities owned or controlled by China (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.R. 10737, sponsored by Rep. Scott Franklin (R-FL-18) — promotes transparency in science under the Environmental Research, Development, and Demonstration Authorization Act of 1978 (Science, Space, and Technology).

H.R. 10738, sponsored by Rep. James Gallagher (R-CA-1) — requires state regulators to consider discounted electric rates for consumers in counties that host certain generation facilities (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10739, sponsored by Rep. Michael Guest (R-MS-3) — encourages qualified individuals to enter the forensic pathology workforce (Energy and Commerce, Ways and Means).

H.R. 10740, sponsored by Rep. William R. Keating (D-MA-9) — designates Ukraine for Temporary Protected Status so certain Ukrainian nationals keep eligibility, with dozens of bipartisan cosponsors (Judiciary).
H.R. 10741, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — aims to expand the supply of child care (Education and Workforce and four other committees).
H.R. 10742, sponsored by Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-8) — directs the Secretary of Defense to report on lessons from defense innovations in the Russia-Ukraine War (Armed Services).

H.R. 10743, sponsored by Rep. Susie Lee (D-NV-3) — ensures Nonprofit Security Grant Program awards are not treated as reimbursements for costs already incurred (Transportation and Infrastructure, Homeland Security).
H.R. 10744, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY-4) — exempts small-scale red meat producers and processors from parts of the Federal Meat Inspection Act (Agriculture).

H.R. 10745, sponsored by Rep. Mary E. Miller (R-IL-15) — would prevent the removal of children from their homes over "sex-rejecting interventions" (Education and Workforce, Judiciary, Ways and Means).
H.R. 10746, sponsored by Rep. Ayanna Pressley (D-MA-7) — requires a reduction of financial-sector emissions to protect financial stability (Financial Services).
H.R. 10747, sponsored by Rep. Raul Ruiz (D-CA-25) — ensures appropriate geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico (Ways and Means, Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10748, sponsored by Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15) — requires a report on security cooperation with Western Balkan countries (Foreign Affairs).
H.R. 10749, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL-25) — authorizes emergency assistance for high-value crop losses (Agriculture).

H.R. 10750, sponsored by Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA-27) — directs the Secretary of the Air Force to create a pilot program for in-space demonstrations of nuclear fission and fusion propulsion (Armed Services).
H.Res. 1606, sponsored by Rep. Becca Balint (D-VT) — supports designating October 24–31, 2026, as "Bat Week" (Agriculture).
H.Res. 1607, sponsored by Rep. Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR-1) — supports designating September 2026 as "National Workforce Development Month" (Education and Workforce).
H.Res. 1608, sponsored by Rep. Judy Chu (D-CA-28) — supports designating October 5, 2026, as "National Beyond the Milky Way Day" (Science, Space, and Technology).
H.Res. 1609, sponsored by Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-6) — honors Marine Corps veteran Nicholas Douglas Quets, offers condolences to his family and condemns cartel violence (Armed Services).
H.Res. 1610, sponsored by Rep. Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY-9) — supports recognizing October 2026 as "World Menopause Awareness Month" (Energy and Commerce and two other committees).
H.Res. 1611, sponsored by Rep. Jim Costa (D-CA-21) — supports designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day" (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.Res. 1612, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — honors Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073 and condemns the attempted terrorist attack on that flight (Foreign Affairs).
H.Res. 1613, sponsored by Rep. Young Kim (R-CA-40) — supports recognizing October 5 as "National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day" (Energy and Commerce).
H.Res. 1614, sponsored by Rep. Glenn Thompson (R-PA-15) — supports designating October 4–10, 2026, as "National 4-H Week" (Education and Workforce, Agriculture).
H.Res. 1615, sponsored by Rep. Norma J. Torres (D-CA-35) — supports designating October 2, 2026, as "Manufacturing Day" (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.Res. 1616, sponsored by Rep. David G. Valadao (R-CA-22) — recognizes the importance of biodiversity conservation, welcomes Armenia as host of the Seventeenth Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity, and supports protection of its sovereign territory (Foreign Affairs).
